q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The authorisation under Article 348(2) of the Constitution for the use of Hindi in the proceedings of a High Court does not extend to any judgment, decree or order of that High Court.
2. Under Article 349 of the Constitution, during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, no Bill relating to the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts could be introduced in Parliament without the previous sanction of the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 348(2) authorisation for Hindi in High Court proceedings expressly does not extend to judgments, decrees or orders, which remain in English. Article 349 barred introduction of any Bill on the language of the Supreme Court and High Courts during the first fifteen years without the previous sanction of the President, so both are correct.

q: Which of the following pairs of an Article of the Constitution and its subject matter is correctly matched?

options.A: Article 345 — Directive for the development of the Hindi language
options.B: Article 346 — Facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
options.C: Article 350 — Language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.D: Article 351 — Directive for the development of the Hindi language

e: Article 351 is the directive for the development and enrichment of Hindi. Article 345 is the official language of a State, Article 346 is communication between the Union and States, and Article 350 is grievance representations, so only the Article 351 pairing is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the commencement of the Constitution, the Eighth Schedule contained 14 languages.
2. At present, the Eighth Schedule contains 22 languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Eighth Schedule originally listed 14 languages at the commencement of the Constitution, and after the 21st, 71st, 92nd and 96th Amendments it now lists 22 languages, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (21st Amendment) Act, 1967.
2. Bodo was added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (71st Amendment) Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (21st Amendment) Act, 1967. Bodo was added by the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003, not the 71st Amendment, which added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes 'proficiency' in Hindi from 'working knowledge' of Hindi for the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976?

options.A: An employee is deemed to have proficiency in Hindi if he has passed the Matriculation or an equivalent or higher examination with Hindi as the medium of examination, whereas working knowledge of Hindi may also be acquired by passing the Pragya examination or by a self-declaration to that effect
options.B: Proficiency in Hindi is acquired only by passing the Pragya examination, whereas working knowledge requires Hindi as a subject at the postgraduate level
options.C: There is no difference between the two expressions; both require passing the Prabodh examination
options.D: Working knowledge of Hindi is the higher standard, and proficiency is merely the ability to read Hindi

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, proficiency is the higher standard, deemed from passing Matriculation or a higher examination with Hindi as the medium of examination; working knowledge can also be acquired by passing Pragya or by a self-declaration, so option A correctly distinguishes the two.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Presidential Order of 1960 on official language was issued after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament on the recommendations of the first Official Language Commission.
2. In-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees by the Presidential Order of 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Presidential Order of 1960 was issued after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament on the first Official Language Commission recommendations, and it made in-service Hindi training compulsory for Central Government employees, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the setting up of the institutions relating to the Official Language?

options.A: Department of Official Language — Central Hindi Directorate — Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology — Kendriya Hindi Samiti
options.B: Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology — Kendriya Hindi Samiti — Central Hindi Directorate — Department of Official Language
options.C: Central Hindi Directorate — Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology — Kendriya Hindi Samiti — Department of Official Language
options.D: Kendriya Hindi Samiti — Central Hindi Directorate — Department of Official Language — Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology

e: The Central Hindi Directorate was set up in 1960, the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology in 1961, the Kendriya Hindi Samiti in 1967 and the Department of Official Language in 1975, giving the order Directorate, Commission, Samiti, Department.

q: A Central Government office has finalised a contract and proposes to issue it in English only, on the ground that the contracting firm is based abroad. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.A: The contract must be issued in both Hindi and English, and the responsibility for ensuring this rests with the officer signing the document
options.B: The contract may be issued in English only, as Section 3(3) does not cover contracts with foreign firms
options.C: The contract may be issued in English only, if the Hindi version is kept in the office file
options.D: The contract must be issued in Hindi only

e: Contracts are expressly among the documents listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, so a contract must be issued in both Hindi and English regardless of the other party, and the officer signing the document is responsible for ensuring this bilingual issue.

q: A citizen sends a letter in Hindi to a Central Government office located in Region 'C'. The dealing clerk proposes to reply in English, as the office is located in a non-Hindi speaking region. The correct position under the Official Language Rules is:

options.A: The reply may be sent in English, Region 'C' being exempt from Hindi correspondence
options.B: The letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, the target for such replies being 100 per cent
options.C: The reply must be sent in the regional language of the State
options.D: The reply may be sent in either language at the discretion of the clerk

e: Rule 5(2) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 and the Annual Programme require that a communication received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, with a 100 per cent target for such replies, irrespective of the Region in which the office is located.

q: A Central Government office in Delhi sends a communication in English to a State Government office located in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such a communication:

options.A: May be sent in English without any accompaniment
options.B: Must be sent in Hindi only, English being prohibited
options.C: Must be returned by the receiving office for want of Hindi
options.D: Must be accompanied by its Hindi translation

e: Under Rule 5 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication to Region A must be in Hindi, and where such a communication is sent in English it must be accompanied by its Hindi translation; Region A covers Hindi-speaking States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.

q: A Central Government office issues a communication in Hindi to an office located in Region 'C'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication:

options.A: Needs no accompaniment, Hindi being the Official Language of the Union
options.B: Must be sent again in the regional language within a week
options.C: Must be accompanied by its English translation
options.D: Must first be approved by the Department of Official Language

e: Under Rule 5 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications to Region C are ordinarily in English, and where a communication is issued in Hindi to an office in Region C it must be accompanied by its English translation.

q: In a Central Government office, 75 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The head of the office proposes to get the office notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976. The correct position is:

options.A: The office cannot be so notified, as notification requires 80 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office can be notified, as 75 per cent is the prescribed threshold
options.C: The office can be notified, as the threshold is only 50 per cent
options.D: Notification under Rule 10(4) depends on the size of the office, not on the proportion of its staff

e: Notification under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 requires that 80 per cent or more of the staff of the office have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. At 75 per cent the threshold is not met, so the office cannot be notified.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 5 from Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Section 5 deals with State Acts, while Section 6 deals with Central Acts
options.B: Section 5 provides that the Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi, while Section 6 makes a corresponding provision for an Act of a State Legislature passed in a language other than Hindi
options.C: Section 5 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 6 deals with rule-making power
options.D: Both Sections deal only with the language of the High Courts

e: Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 makes the Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance published under the authority of the President the authoritative Hindi text, while Section 6 makes the corresponding provision for State Acts passed in a language other than Hindi.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act vests in the Central Government.
2. The Official Languages Act, 1963 came into force on 26th January, 1965.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 vests rule-making power in the Central Government, and the Act, though enacted in 1963, was brought into force on 26th January, 1965, the date from which the constitutional fifteen-year period expired, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the use of Hindi for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court may be authorised by the Governor of the State with the previous consent of the President.
2. Where such use is authorised, every such judgment, decree or order must be accompanied by a translation thereof in English issued under the authority of the High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 permits the Governor, with the previous consent of the President, to authorise Hindi in addition to English for judgments, decrees or orders of the High Court, and every such judgment, decree or order must be accompanied by an English translation issued under the authority of the High Court, so both are correct.

q:
Match the Sections of the Official Languages Act, 1963 with their subject matter:
1. Section 4, 2. Section 5, 3. Section 7, 4. Section 8
(a) Power of the Central Government to make rules, (b) Authoritative Hindi text of Central Acts, (c) Committee of Parliament on Official Language, (d) Use of Hindi in judgments of High Courts
e: In the Official Languages Act, 1963, Section 4 is the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, Section 5 is the authoritative Hindi text of Central Acts, Section 7 is the use of Hindi in High Court judgments, and Section 8 is the Central Government rule-making power, giving 1-(c), 2-(b), 3-(d), 4-(a).

q: A despatch clerk is checking compliance with Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963. Which one of the following is NOT among the documents required to be issued in both Hindi and English under that Section?

options.A: The service book of a Government employee
options.C: Licences and permits issued by the office
options.D: Tender forms issued by the office

e: Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 covers resolutions, general orders, rules, notifications, contracts, licences, permits, tender notices and forms, but a Government employee service book is not in that list, so it is the document not required to be issued bilingually under that Section.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Rules, 1976 apply to the whole of India except the State of Tamil Nadu.
2. The Committee of Parliament on Official Language functioning at present is constituted under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Official Language Rules, 1976 extend to the whole of India except Tamil Nadu, and the present Committee of Parliament on Official Language is the statutory committee constituted under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following statements about communications under the Official Language Rules, 1976 is correct?

options.A: Communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another must invariably be in Hindi only
options.B: Communications between Central Government offices situated in Region 'A' may be in the regional language only
options.C: Communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or English, whereas communications between Central Government offices situated in Region 'A' (other than those between a Ministry/Department and its attached or subordinate offices) shall be in Hindi
options.D: Communications from a Ministry to its attached offices in Region 'A' must invariably be wholly in Hindi, with no proportion prescribed

e: Under Rule 5 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between one Central Ministry or Department and another may be in Hindi or in English, while communications between Central Government offices in Region A, other than between a Ministry or Department and its attached or subordinate offices, are to be in Hindi, for which a proportion is prescribed.

q: Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, which of the following pairings of target is correct?

options.A: Correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' — 90 per cent
options.B: Correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' — 90 per cent
options.C: Correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' — 90 per cent
options.D: Noting on files in Hindi — 55 per cent

e: The Annual Programme fixes the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region B at 90 per cent, against 100 per cent for Region A and 55 per cent for Region C; the noting target is not 55 per cent in the pairing offered, so only the Region B pairing is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands is placed in Region 'A'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the Union Territory of Chandigarh is placed in Region 'B'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: In the Official Language Rules, 1976, the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands is included in Region A along with Delhi and the Hindi-speaking States, and the Union Territory of Chandigarh is placed in Region B, so both statements are correct.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the cities of Jaipur, Nagpur and Kochi are respectively located in:
e: Jaipur is in Rajasthan, a Region A State; Nagpur is in Maharashtra, a Region B State; and Kochi is in Kerala, a Region C State, under the regional classification in the Official Language Rules, 1976.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Punjab is placed in Region 'B'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Goa is placed in Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Punjab is placed in Region B under the Official Language Rules, 1976, along with Gujarat and Maharashtra, and Goa is placed in Region C, so both statements are correct.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Receipt" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, a Receipt, the written acknowledgement of money or goods received, is Raseed; Pramanak is a voucher and Mang Patra is an indent.

q:
Consider the following statements about the public interface at railway stations:
1. Announcements for the guidance of passengers at railway stations are made in three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English.
2. The reservation and cancellation requisition forms supplied to passengers are printed in Hindi and English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: At railway stations, passenger announcements are made trilingually in the regional language, Hindi and English, and reservation and cancellation requisition forms supplied to passengers are printed bilingually in Hindi and English, so both statements are correct under railway Rajbhasha practice.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained in Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form.
2. For doing Hindi work on computers in Central Government offices, a Unicode-compliant font should be used.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Department of Official Language instructions require Central Government websites to be bilingual in Hindi and English, and Hindi work on computers is to be done in Unicode so that text is standard, searchable and exchangeable, so both statements are correct.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Capital" (funds) is:
e: In standard Hindi accounting terminology, Capital in the sense of funds invested is Punji; Bhandar is stores, Rajaswa is revenue and Vyay is expenditure.

q:
Match the institutions with the year of their establishment:
1. Central Hindi Directorate, 2. Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology, 3. Central Translation Bureau, 4. Department of Official Language
(a) 1975, (b) 1971, (c) 1961, (d) 1960
e: The Central Hindi Directorate was established in 1960, the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology in 1961, the Central Translation Bureau in 1971 and the Department of Official Language in 1975, giving 1-(d), 2-(c), 3-(b), 4-(a).

q:
Match the institutions with their principal function relating to the Official Language:
1. Central Translation Bureau, 2. Official Language Wing of the Legislative Department, 3. Central Hindi Directorate, 4. Central Hindi Training Institute
(a) In-service Hindi training and conduct of the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations, (b) Correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, (c) Translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts, (d) Translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material
e: The Central Translation Bureau translates non-statutory codes, manuals and forms; the Official Language Wing of the Legislative Department translates Bills and Central Acts; the Central Hindi Directorate runs the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya correspondence courses; and the Central Hindi Training Institute gives in-service training and conducts those examinations, giving 1-(d), 2-(c), 3-(b), 4-(a).

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi was established in the year 1985.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi), Agra functions under the Ministry of Education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi was set up in 1985 to impart in-service Hindi training and conduct Hindi Teaching Scheme examinations, and the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan at Agra functions under the Ministry of Education, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted in a town or city which has ten or more Central Government offices.
2. Meetings of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee are normally held twice a year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted in a town or city having ten or more Central Government offices to coordinate implementation among them, and its meetings are normally held twice a year, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office is chaired by the head of the office.
2. Meetings of the Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office are normally held every quarter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office is chaired by the head of that office and normally meets every quarter to review progress and decide corrective action, so both statements are correct.

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination through his own efforts, by self-study, without undergoing the prescribed training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. Under the incentive scheme, he is entitled to:

options.D: No incentive, as training is compulsory for any award

e: An employee who passes Pragya through self-study, without undergoing the prescribed training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, is entitled to a lumpsum award under the incentive provisions, in place of the personal pay admissible to trained employees.

q: An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 92 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes Hindi stenography
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay for 24 months
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks

e: The cash award threshold for the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is 90 per cent or more marks, so an employee securing 92 per cent qualifies for the cash award; no stenography pass or 95 per cent threshold is required.

q: Which of the following pairings of marks in the Pragya examination and the cash award admissible is correct?
e: Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi Pakhwada is observed in Central Government offices every year from 14th September to 28th September.
2. Hindi Diwas was celebrated for the first time in the year 1953.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Hindi Pakhwada is observed every year from 14th September, Hindi Diwas, to 28th September in Central Government offices, and Hindi Diwas was first celebrated in 1953, four years after the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language on 14th September, 1949, so both are correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two awards of the Department of Official Language?

options.A: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar is given for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy by Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks, while the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is given for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects
options.B: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar is given for original book writing in Hindi, while the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is given for implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.C: Both the awards are given only to individual employees for noting and drafting in Hindi
options.D: Both the awards are given only to Zonal Railways and Divisions

e: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar rewards excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy by Ministries and Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks, while the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar rewards original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects, which is the correct distinction between the two Department of Official Language awards.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Voucher" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, a Voucher, the document evidencing a payment, is Pramanak; Raseed is a receipt, Mang Patra is an indent and Talpat is a trial balance.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English accounting term "Trial Balance" is:
e: In standard Hindi accounting terminology, a Trial Balance, the statement of debit and credit balances drawn from the ledger, is Talpat; Tulan Patra is a balance sheet and Khata Bahi is a ledger.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Indent" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, an Indent, a requisition for stores or material, is Mang Patra; Anugyapti is a licence and Aarop Patra is a charge sheet.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Commission to be constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution consists of a Chairman and other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule.
2. After considering the report of the Committee of Parliament on the recommendations of the Official Language Commission, directions in accordance with that report are issued by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 344(2) lists the matters on which the Official Language Commission recommends, including the progressive use of Hindi and the form of numerals, and Article 344(3) requires the Commission to have due regard to the industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and the just claims of non-Hindi speaking areas in public services; the President issues directions after considering the Parliamentary Committee report, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the proviso to Article 345 of the Constitution, until the Legislature of a State by law otherwise provides, English continues to be used for those official purposes of the State for which it was being used immediately before the commencement of the Constitution.
2. Under the proviso to Article 346 of the Constitution, if two or more States agree that Hindi shall be the official language for communication between such States, Hindi may be used for that purpose.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The proviso to Article 345 continues English for State official purposes until the State Legislature otherwise provides, and the proviso to Article 346 permits two or more States to agree to use Hindi for communication between themselves, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all Bills introduced in Parliament or in a State Legislature, and of all Acts passed by them, shall be in English.
2. Under Article 348(3) of the Constitution, where a State Legislature has prescribed a language other than English for use in Bills introduced in, or Acts passed by, that Legislature, a translation of the same in English, published under the authority of the Governor, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 348(1) requires authoritative texts of Bills and Acts of Parliament and State Legislatures to be in English until Parliament otherwise provides, and Article 348(3) deems an English translation of a State Bill or Act published under the Governor authority to be its authoritative English text, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court has been authorised by the Governor with the previous consent of the President in the State of Rajasthan.
2. The use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court has been authorised by the Governor with the previous consent of the President in the State of West Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Hindi has been authorised in High Court proceedings by the Governor with the previous consent of the President under Article 348(2) in States such as Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar. No such authorisation exists for West Bengal, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes clause (2) from clause (3) of Article 343 of the Constitution?

options.A: Clause (2) empowers Parliament to provide by law for the use of English after fifteen years, while clause (3) empowers the President to authorise the use of Hindi during the first fifteen years
options.B: Clause (2) empowers the President, during the first fifteen years, to authorise by order the use of Hindi in addition to English, and of the Devanagari form of numerals in addition to the international form of Indian numerals, while clause (3) empowers Parliament to provide by law, even after fifteen years, for the use of English or the Devanagari form of numerals for specified purposes
options.C: Both the clauses empower only the President to issue orders about the use of numerals
options.D: Clause (2) deals with the language of the High Courts, while clause (3) deals with the language of Parliament

e: Article 343(2) empowers the President during the first fifteen years to authorise by order Hindi in addition to English, and Devanagari numerals in addition to the international form of Indian numerals, for specified purposes; Article 343(3) empowers Parliament to provide by law even after fifteen years for English or Devanagari numerals, so option B is correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 345 from Article 346 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 345 deals with communication between two States, while Article 346 deals with the official language of a State
options.B: Both the Articles deal only with the language to be used in the Supreme Court
options.C: Article 345 empowers a State Legislature to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the official language of that State, while Article 346 provides that the language for the time being authorised for use in the Union for its official purposes shall be the official language for communication between the Union and a State, or between one State and another
options.D: Article 345 deals with the development of Hindi, while Article 346 deals with instruction in the mother tongue

e: Article 345 empowers a State Legislature to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the official language of the State, while Article 346 provides that the language authorised for the official purposes of the Union shall be the language for communication between the Union and a State and between States, so option C is correct.

q: Of the 30 members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, the members drawn from the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha respectively number:
e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 consists of 30 members, 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, elected by proportional representation by single transferable vote.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The authoritative text of the Constitution of India in the Hindi language is published under the authority of the President in accordance with Article 394A, which was inserted by the Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987.
2. The Munshi-Ayyangar formula on the official language is named after K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 394A, inserted by the Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987, provides for publication under the President authority of the authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution, and the compromise on official language in the Constituent Assembly is known as the Munshi-Ayyangar formula, after K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Languages Act, 1963 received the assent of the President on 10th May, 1963.
2. The Official Language Resolution, embodying the policy for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, was adopted by Parliament in the year 1968.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Official Languages Act, 1963 received the assent of the President on 10th May, 1963, and the Official Language Resolution setting out the policy for the progressive use of Hindi was adopted by both Houses of Parliament in 1968, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission), appointed in 1955, submitted its report to the President in the year 1956.
2. The Presidential Order based on the recommendations of the first Official Language Commission, issued after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament, was issued in the year 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The first Official Language Commission under B. G. Kher, appointed in 1955, submitted its report in 1956, and the Presidential Order of 1960 was issued on its recommendations after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following statements about the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is FALSE?

options.A: At the commencement of the Constitution, it contained 14 languages
options.C: It is referred to in Articles 344 and 351 of the Constitution
options.D: English is one of the languages included in it

e: The Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages and now has 22, and it is referred to in Articles 344 and 351. English is not a language included in the Eighth Schedule, so that statement is the false one.

q:
Match the languages included in the Eighth Schedule with the scripts in which they are written:
1. Santhali, 2. Bodo, 3. Kashmiri, 4. Manipuri (traditional script)
(a) Devanagari, (b) Meitei Mayek, (c) Ol Chiki, (d) Perso-Arabic
e: Santhali is written in the Ol Chiki script devised for it, Bodo is written in Devanagari, Kashmiri is written in the Perso-Arabic script, and Manipuri traditional script is Meitei Mayek, giving 1-(c), 2-(a), 3-(d), 4-(b).

q:
Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. Hindi is the mother tongue of about 43.6 per cent of the population of India.
2. Bengali is the second most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: As per the Census of India, 2011 language data, Hindi is the mother tongue of about 43.6 per cent of the population, the largest share, and Bengali is the second most widely spoken mother tongue, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Devanagari script, in which Hindi is written, is also known as Nagari.
2. The Devanagari script has evolved from the ancient script known as Brahmi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Devanagari, the script of Hindi prescribed in Article 343, is also called Nagari, and like other major Indian scripts it has evolved from the ancient Brahmi script, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Gujarat is placed in Region 'B'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of West Bengal is placed in Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Gujarat is placed in Region B under the Official Language Rules, 1976, along with Maharashtra and Punjab, while West Bengal is placed in Region C, so both statements are correct.

q: A Central Government office in Delhi sends an ordinary communication to a State Government office located in Region 'B'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such a communication shall ordinarily be in:

options.A: English only, Region 'B' being a non-Hindi region for all purposes
options.B: The regional language of the State concerned
options.D: Hindi and the regional language, in equal proportion

e: Under Rule 5 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region B are ordinarily in Hindi, unlike Region C where English is ordinarily used.

q: A Central Government office issues a communication in English to a person (a member of the public) in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication:

options.A: May be issued in English without any accompaniment
options.B: Must be accompanied by its Hindi translation
options.C: Must be withdrawn and re-issued in the regional language
options.D: Must be approved in advance by the Department of Official Language

e: Under Rule 5 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication in English issued to a person in Region A must be accompanied by its Hindi translation, since Region A is the Hindi-speaking region where correspondence is to be in Hindi.

q: A Central Government office has to correspond with the embassy of a foreign country located in India. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, such correspondence is conducted in:

options.B: Hindi and the language of that country
options.C: The regional language of the State in which the embassy is located

e: Correspondence with foreign Governments, their embassies and international organisations is conducted in English under the official language policy and the Official Language Rules framework, not in Hindi or a regional language.

q: For working out the percentage of Hindi correspondence in its Quarterly Progress Report, a Central Government office counts as Hindi correspondence every letter of which a Hindi version was issued, including letters first drafted in English and then translated into Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: The method is correct, as every letter issued in Hindi counts as Hindi correspondence
options.B: The method is incorrect, as only letters originally written and issued in Hindi are counted as Hindi correspondence; an English draft merely translated into Hindi is not so counted
options.C: The method is correct only for offices located in Region 'A'
options.D: Translated letters are counted at half their number for this purpose

e: For Quarterly Progress Report purposes, only letters originally written in Hindi and issued in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence. A letter drafted in English and merely translated into Hindi before issue is not counted as correspondence originating in Hindi, so the office method is incorrect.

q: A Central Government office finalises a press communique and proposes to issue it in English only, as it is meant for the English newspapers. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.A: The press communique may be issued in English only
options.B: The press communique must be issued in Hindi only
options.C: The press communique must be issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: The press communique may be issued in English only if its Hindi version is retained on the office file

e: Press communiques and press notes are among the documents listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, so a press communique must be issued in both Hindi and English, whatever the intended newspapers.

q: A Central Government office gets its letter-heads printed in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the letter-heads used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in:

options.B: Hindi only, as proposed by the office
options.D: Hindi, English and the regional language

e: Rule 11 of the Official Language Rules, 1976 and Department of Official Language instructions require letter-heads, printed forms and similar stationery of Central Government offices to be printed bilingually in Hindi and English, with Hindi taking precedence in order, not in Hindi alone.

q: A Central Government office purchases books for its office library and proposes to spend the entire amount on English books. Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, at least what proportion of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries should be spent on Hindi books?
e: The Annual Programme requires that at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries be spent on Hindi books, to build up Hindi reference and reading material in offices.

q: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language is to visit a Central Government office for inspection of the implementation of the Official Language Policy. Before the visit, detailed information about the implementation in that office is obtained by the Committee through:

options.A: The Annual Assessment Report of the Department of Official Language
options.B: A prescribed questionnaire (Prashnavali) filled in by the office
options.C: The Quarterly Progress Report of the controlling Ministry
options.D: An inspection by the Central Translation Bureau

e: Before inspecting an office, the Committee of Parliament on Official Language obtains detailed information on the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that office through a prescribed questionnaire, called Prashnavali, filled in and furnished by the office.

q: A citizen residing in Region 'C' submits a representation to a Central Government office in English. The office returns it, saying that representations are accepted only in Hindi. The correct position under the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office is right, as representations must be submitted in Hindi only
options.B: The office is right, as the citizen resides in Region 'C'
options.C: The office is wrong, as a member of the public may submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or in English
options.D: The representation should have been submitted in the regional language of the State

e: Rule 5 of the Official Language Rules, 1976 gives a member of the public the choice to submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or in English, and representations in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi; the office cannot refuse an English representation or insist on Hindi only.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The three-language formula for school education was adopted as a part of the National Policy on Education, 1968.
2. Under the three-language formula, the three languages to be studied in the Hindi-speaking States are Hindi, English and a modern Indian language, preferably one of the southern languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The three-language formula formed part of the National Policy on Education, 1968, and in Hindi-speaking States it prescribes Hindi, English and a modern Indian language, preferably a southern language, as the three languages of school study, so both statements are correct.

q:
Match the World Hindi Conferences with the places where they were held:
1. First World Hindi Conference, 2. Third World Hindi Conference, 3. Tenth World Hindi Conference, 4. Twelfth World Hindi Conference
(a) Bhopal, (b) Nadi (Fiji), (c) Nagpur, (d) New Delhi
e: The First World Hindi Conference was held at Nagpur in 1975, the Third at New Delhi in 1983, the Tenth at Bhopal in 2015 and the Twelfth at Nadi in Fiji in 2023, giving 1-(c), 2-(d), 3-(a), 4-(b).

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Hindi Diwas from World Hindi Day?

options.A: Hindi Diwas, observed on 14th September, is organised under the aegis of the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, while World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January, is celebrated by the Ministry of External Affairs through the Indian Missions abroad
options.B: Hindi Diwas is celebrated only abroad, while World Hindi Day is celebrated only in India
options.C: Both are observed on 14th September, one by the Department of Official Language and the other by the Ministry of External Affairs
options.D: World Hindi Day, observed on 14th September, marks the adoption of Hindi as the Official Language in 1949

e: Hindi Diwas on 14th September, marking the 1949 adoption of Hindi as official language, is organised in India under the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, while World Hindi Day on 10th January is promoted by the Ministry of External Affairs through Indian Missions abroad, so option A is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, a leading organisation for the promotion of Hindi, was founded in the year 1910.
2. The headquarters of the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan is located at Prayagraj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, a leading voluntary organisation for the promotion of Hindi language and literature, was founded in 1910 and has its headquarters at Prayagraj, so both statements are correct.

q:
Match the institutions with the year of their establishment:
1. Hindi Teaching Scheme, 2. Office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities, 3. Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi), Agra, 4. Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysuru
(a) 1969, (b) 1955, (c) 1957, (d) 1960
e: The Hindi Teaching Scheme dates to 1955 in its organised in-service form, the Office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957 under Article 350B, the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan at Agra in 1960 and the Central Institute of Indian Languages at Mysuru in 1969, giving 1-(b), 2-(c), 3-(d), 4-(a).

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Hindi Directorate was established in the year 1960.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra was also established in the year 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Central Hindi Directorate was established on 1st March, 1960 for the promotion and propagation of Hindi, and the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan at Agra was also established in 1960 for teaching Hindi to non-Hindi speakers, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Besides translation work, the Central Translation Bureau also conducts translation training programmes for the translators of Central Government offices.
2. The Central Translation Bureau functions as a subordinate office of the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Besides translating non-statutory material for Central Government offices, the Central Translation Bureau conducts translation training programmes for translators, and it functions as a subordinate office of the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following statements about the Central Translation Bureau is FALSE?

options.A: It was set up in the year 1971
options.B: Its headquarters is located at New Delhi
options.C: It is mainly responsible for the translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices
options.D: It functions under the Ministry of Education

e: The Central Translation Bureau was set up in 1971 with headquarters at New Delhi for translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material, but it functions under the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Ministry of Education, so that statement is false.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology from the Central Translation Bureau?

options.A: The Commission evolves and defines scientific and technical terms in Hindi and other Indian languages and publishes glossaries and definitional dictionaries, while the Bureau translates codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices
options.B: The Commission translates codes and manuals, while the Bureau evolves scientific and technical terminology
options.C: Both the bodies only conduct the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.D: The Commission is a railway body, while the Bureau functions only for the State Governments

e: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology evolves and defines scientific and technical terms in Hindi and other Indian languages and publishes glossaries and definitional dictionaries, while the Central Translation Bureau translates codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material, so option A correctly distinguishes them.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) from the Central Official Language Implementation Committee?

options.A: Both the committees are chaired by the Prime Minister
options.B: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister, while the Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language
options.C: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language, while the Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister
options.D: Both the committees function only at the level of Zonal Railways

e: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti is the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi and is chaired by the Prime Minister, while the Central Official Language Implementation Committee, which reviews implementation across Ministries, is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language, so option B is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The secretariat of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is provided by the Department of Official Language.
2. The Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Department of Official Language provides the secretariat for the Committee of Parliament on Official Language constituted under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, and the Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry is chaired by the Minister in charge of the Ministry.
2. The Hindi Salahakar Samiti of the Ministry of Railways functions mainly to advise the Ministry on matters relating to the progressive use of Hindi and the implementation of the Official Language Policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Hindi Salahakar Samiti of a Union Ministry is chaired by the Minister in charge of that Ministry, and the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti advises the Ministry of Railways on the progressive use of Hindi and implementation of the Official Language Policy, so both statements are correct.

q: For Hindi (Devanagari) typing on computers in Central Government offices, the keyboard layout adopted as the standard is known as:
e: For Hindi typing on computers in Central Government offices, the InScript keyboard layout, based on a common layout for Indian scripts and supported by Unicode, is the standard adopted layout, not Remington or phonetic layouts.

q: To enable employees who possess knowledge of Hindi but hesitate to use it in their official work, an office organises a programme giving them practical training in doing noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi. Such a programme is known as a:
e: A Hindi Workshop, or Hindi Karyashala, gives employees who know Hindi but hesitate to use it practical training in noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi, typically over a few days, which is distinct from Pakhwada celebrations, seminars and the Prabodh language course.

q: An employee is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, to be imparted during office hours. In this case:

options.A: The employee has to pay the prescribed fee and take leave for the training period
options.B: The training is free of cost and the training period is treated as on duty
options.C: The training period is treated as leave without pay
options.D: Only half of the training period is treated as on duty

e: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme during office hours is free of cost to the employee, and the period spent in training and examinations is treated as on duty, so no fee or leave is required.

q:
Match the languages with the year in which they were accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India:
1. Tamil, 2. Sanskrit, 3. Telugu, 4. Odia
(a) 2008, (b) 2014, (c) 2004, (d) 2005
e: Tamil was declared a classical language in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005, Telugu in 2008 and Odia in 2014 by the Government of India, giving 1-(c), 2-(d), 3-(a), 4-(b).

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Income" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, Income is Aay; Vyay is expenditure, Labh is profit and Rin is a loan or debt.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Profit" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, Profit is Labh; Hani is loss and Mulya Hras is depreciation.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Loss" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, Loss is Hani; Labh is profit, Katauti is a deduction or cut and Bakaya is arrears or an outstanding amount.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Fee" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, a Fee charged for a service is Shulk; Kar is a tax, Bhatta is an allowance and Maanadeya is an honorarium.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Rent" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, Rent is Kiraya; Rajaswa is revenue, Agrim is an advance and Anudan is a grant.

q:
Match the States with their official languages:
1. Karnataka, 2. Assam, 3. Punjab, 4. Odisha
(a) Assamese, (b) Odia, (c) Kannada, (d) Punjabi
e: The official language of Karnataka is Kannada, of Assam is Assamese, of Punjab is Punjabi and of Odisha is Odia, as adopted by those States under Article 345, giving 1-(c), 2-(a), 3-(d), 4-(b).

q:
Match the States with the language of their subordinate (district) courts:
1. Maharashtra, 2. Punjab, 3. Bihar, 4. Uttarakhand
(a) Punjabi, (b) Marathi, (c) Hindi, (d) Hindi
e: Subordinate courts use Marathi in Maharashtra, Punjabi in Punjab, and Hindi in Bihar and in Uttarakhand, giving 1-(b), 2-(a), 3-(c), 4-(d).

q:
Match the languages with the year in which they were accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India:
1. Sanskrit, 2. Kannada, 3. Malayalam, 4. Odia
(a) 2013, (b) 2005, (c) 2014, (d) 2008
e: Sanskrit was declared a classical language in 2005, Kannada in 2008, Malayalam in 2013 and Odia in 2014 by the Government of India, giving 1-(b), 2-(d), 3-(a), 4-(c).

q:
Match the World Hindi Conferences with the places where they were held:
1. Second World Hindi Conference, 2. Fifth World Hindi Conference, 3. Sixth World Hindi Conference, 4. Seventh World Hindi Conference
(a) London, (b) Paramaribo (Suriname), (c) Port Louis (Mauritius), (d) Port of Spain (Trinidad and Tobago)
e: The Second World Hindi Conference was held at Port Louis in Mauritius, the Fifth at Port of Spain in Trinidad and Tobago, the Sixth in London and the Seventh at Paramaribo in Suriname, giving 1-(c), 2-(d), 3-(a), 4-(b).

q:
Match the languages with the language family or description with which they are associated:
1. Bodo, 2. Santhali, 3. Telugu, 4. Kashmiri
(a) Austroasiatic (Munda) family, (b) Dardic group, (c) Tibeto-Burman family, (d) Popularly known as the 'Italian of the East'
e: Bodo belongs to the Tibeto-Burman family, Santhali to the Austroasiatic (Munda) family, Telugu is popularly called the Italian of the East for its vowel-ending words, and Kashmiri belongs to the Dardic group, giving 1-(c), 2-(a), 3-(d), 4-(b).

q:
Match the celebrated Hindi works with their authors:
1. Godan, 2. Madhushala, 3. Kamayani, 4. Rashmirathi
(a) Jaishankar Prasad, (b) Munshi Premchand, (c) Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, (d) Harivansh Rai Bachchan
e: Godan is by Munshi Premchand, Madhushala by Harivansh Rai Bachchan, Kamayani by Jaishankar Prasad and Rashmirathi by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, giving 1-(b), 2-(d), 3-(a), 4-(c).

q:
Match the institutions with their principal function relating to the Official Language:
1. Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology, 2. Central Hindi Directorate, 3. Regional Implementation Offices of the Department of Official Language, 4. Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi), Agra
(a) Conducting the correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, (b) Teaching Hindi to non-Hindi speaking Indian and foreign learners, training of Hindi teachers and research in Hindi, (c) Evolving scientific and technical terms in Hindi and other Indian languages and publishing glossaries, (d) Monitoring and inspecting the implementation of the Official Language Policy in Central Government offices in their respective regions
e: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology evolves scientific and technical terms and publishes glossaries; the Central Hindi Directorate conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya correspondence courses; Regional Implementation Offices monitor and inspect implementation in their regions; and the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, Agra teaches Hindi to non-Hindi speaking and foreign learners and trains Hindi teachers, giving 1-(c), 2-(a), 3-(d), 4-(b).

q:
Match the events relating to the Official Language with the year in which they took place:
1. First celebration of Hindi Diwas, 2. Appointment of the first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission), 3. Establishment of the Sahitya Akademi, 4. Adoption of the Official Language Resolution by Parliament
(a) 1955, (b) 1968, (c) 1953, (d) 1954
e: Hindi Diwas was first celebrated in 1953, the first Official Language Commission was appointed in 1955, the Sahitya Akademi was established in 1954 and the Official Language Resolution was adopted by Parliament in 1968, giving 1-(c), 2-(a), 3-(d), 4-(b).

q:
Match the Rajbhasha awards with the sphere for which they are given:
1. Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar, 2. Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar, 3. Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield, 4. Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield
(a) Original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects, (b) Excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy by Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks, (c) The best (Adarsh) Division in Regions 'A' and 'B' on Indian Railways, (d) The Zonal Railway adjudged the best in implementation of the Official Language Policy
e: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar is for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy by Ministries, undertakings and banks; the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is for original Hindi book writing; the Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield goes to the best Zonal Railway; and the Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield goes to the best Adarsh Division in Regions A and B, giving 1-(b), 2-(a), 3-(d), 4-(c).

q:
Match the languages included in the Eighth Schedule with the scripts in which they are written:
1. Punjabi, 2. Urdu, 3. Nepali, 4. Sindhi
(a) Devanagari script, (b) Gurmukhi script, (c) Both the Perso-Arabic and the Devanagari scripts, (d) Perso-Arabic script
e: Punjabi is written in the Gurmukhi script, Urdu in the Perso-Arabic script, Nepali in the Devanagari script, and Sindhi in both the Perso-Arabic and Devanagari scripts, giving 1-(b), 2-(d), 3-(a), 4-(c).

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 344(2) of the Constitution, the Official Language Commission makes recommendations to the President as to, among other things, the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union and the form of numerals to be used.
2. In making its recommendations, the Commission is required to have due regard to the industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and the just claims and interests of persons belonging to the non-Hindi speaking areas in respect of public services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 344(2) requires the Official Language Commission to recommend on the progressive use of Hindi, restrictions on English and the form of numerals, among other matters, and Article 344(3) requires it to have due regard to the industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and the just claims and interests of non-Hindi speaking areas in public services, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi is to draw for its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages.
2. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi is to be enriched by assimilating the forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule, without interfering with its genius.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 351 directs that Hindi be developed so as to serve as a medium of expression for the composite culture of India, drawing for its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages, and enriching it by assimilating forms, style and expressions from Hindustani and the Eighth Schedule languages without interfering with its genius, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, English is used for communication between the Union and a State which has not adopted Hindi as its official language.
2. Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, Hindi is used for communication between the Union and a State which has adopted Hindi as its official language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides that communication between the Union and a State is in English where the State has not adopted Hindi as its official language, and in Hindi where the State has adopted Hindi, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The report of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is submitted to the President, who causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all the State Governments.
2. The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the Committee of Parliament on Official Language submits its report to the President, who causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all State Governments, and the Chairman of the Committee is elected by its members from amongst themselves, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Trains at a Glance', the All India Railway Time Table published by the Indian Railways, is published in Hindi and English.
2. The reservation charts displayed at railway stations are printed in three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Trains at a Glance, the All India Railway Time Table, is published bilingually in Hindi and English, and reservation charts displayed at railway stations are printed trilingually in the regional language, Hindi and English for passenger convenience, so both statements are correct.
